Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)

variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

V_eff = V_b + Σ V_i · Kp_i

within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS

1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes)
2. Compute graph Laplacian
3. Extract 7 eigenvectors via deflated power iteration
4. Map eigenvectors to octonion basis (ψ_k ↔ e_k)
5. Compute G₂ 3-form on the eigenvector frame
6. Compute SU(3) branching quality
7. Run null model (random SO(7) rotations)
8. Compare observed vs null → p-value estimate

T3: Null distribution has lower mean |φ| than observed

T5: Associator deviation field computable on extracted frame

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_layout_shadows_user_field_name`. A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,. description: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
comments: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling.
`ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout —
value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
before any user struct is registered. `field_idx_from_name_simple` resolves a
field *name* to a slot by scanning the whole table in order and taking the
first hit in any struct, and that path is what runs whenever the base is not
a typed local: `arr[i].f` reaches it because array locals record a length but
no element type.
So `ext[0].value` resolved to Knowledge's slot 0 — the same slot as `oid` —
and `ext[0].value = val_buf` overwrote the `oid` written just before it. Both
reads then went to slot 0 too, so `value` read back correct while `oid`
returned `value`'s bytes: a silent wrong answer at rc=0, with no diagnostic.
The trigger was the identifier, not the shape. The same program with the
field named `val` was always correct, at any struct size, array length or
index form — which is why size- and index-threshold hypotheses all died.
Guard all three preseeded names. Anything reading its sibling's data here
means the synthetic layout is shadowing user layouts again.
Honest scope: CI runs this suite under souc-stage2, which never carried the
defect, so this file is green either way there — it is the readable witness,
not the guard. The discriminating gate is the `knowledge_field_shadow` case
in tests/madaros/source_to_elf/manifest.tsv, which compiles with Madaros and
was measured red before this fix and green after.

description: PR #2515 review round 2, finding B (comment_id 4089110697): the specializer's `spec_call_expr_callee_name` (self-hosted/check/specializer.sio) used to treat a multi-segment turbofish path's capitalization alone as
comments: PR #2515 review round 2, finding B (comment_id 4089110697): the
specializer's `spec_call_expr_callee_name` (self-hosted/check/specializer.sio)
used to treat a multi-segment turbofish path's capitalization alone as
module evidence -- an uppercase-first-byte root meant "Type::method,
leave alone", a lowercase root meant "must be a module-qualified free-fn
call, rewrite to the bare terminal symbol". That is unsound: a
lowercase-named struct is legal Sounio (see
tests/multimodule/private_fn_identity/reserved/pfi_res_b.sio's
`struct helper_`), so a lowercase-rooted `Type::assoc_fn::<T>(..)` path
could be misread as a qualified free-fn call and have its whole path
collapsed by spec_rewrite_call_mut to the bare monomorphized `assoc_fn`
symbol -- silently accepting an invalid/misresolved namespace.
`wrap_` here is a lowercase-named generic struct with a generic
associated (not instance) function, called through its path with an
explicit turbofish (`wrap_::make::<i64>(..)`) -- the exact shape the
unsound heuristic could misfire on, since `wrap_` is never `use`d as a
module anywhere (there is nothing to `use`; this is single-file). The
fixed specializer only rewrites a multi-segment turbofish path to a bare
free-fn call when the qualifier resolves against real `use` data
(spec_path_qualifier_all_modules_known); since `wrap_` is not a
`use`-declared module, this path is left alone for ordinary
Type::method / associated-call resolution instead.

comments: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 — cross-check of Gresnigt's three generation-octonions + an explicit G₂
(COLOR-side) monomial automorphism permuting them. Executed against the primary source.
Gresnigt (EPJC 2019/2024; arXiv:2306.13098) builds three fermion generations from three octonion
subalgebras of the sedenions 𝕊 sharing a common quaternion, cyclically related by the family S₃.
The paper's three copies (its basis, App. A) are, as index sets:
sharing the quaternion ℍ = ⟨e₄,e₈,e₁₂⟩ = {4,8,12}.
This test certifies, in this repo's Cayley-Dickson convention:
(a) each 𝕆_i is a genuine (zero-divisor-free) octonion, all three ambient-equivalent (each has 6
non-anticommuting internal left-mult pairs in the 16-dim Cℓ(8));  ℍ = 𝕆₁∩𝕆₂∩𝕆₃ = {4,8,12};
(b) the pure 3-cycle φ = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇)(e₉e₁₀e₁₁)(e₁₃e₁₄e₁₅) [all signs +1, fixing e₀,e₄,e₈,e₁₂]
is a genuine algebra automorphism of 𝕊 (all 256 products), of order 3, cyclically permuting
𝕆₁→𝕆₂→𝕆₃ and fixing ℍ and e₈;
(c) φ = g ⊕ g is DIAGONAL under 𝕊 = 𝕆 ⊕ 𝕆·e₈ with g = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇) an automorphism of the base
octonion {e₁..e₇} — so φ ∈ G₂ = Aut(𝕆).
HONEST BOUNDARY (this is NOT a physics bridge). Because φ ∈ G₂ and G₂ ⊃ SU(3)_color, φ is a
COLOR-sector operation. It is NOT Gresnigt's family S₃: by Brown's theorem Aut(𝕊)=G₂×S₃, and the
family S₃ is precisely the direct factor DISJOINT from G₂ (non-monomial) — used exactly so that
family ≠ color. This brick therefore does NOT connect the zero-divisor monomial-168 to fermion
generations, and does NOT amend Erratum E1 (which correctly places the monomial-168 inside G₂). It
reproduces the paper's octonion triple and exhibits the G₂/color realization of their 3-set
permutation — nothing more. A genuine bridge would require building the fermion ideals and showing
Brown's S₃ acts on those states as a monomial-168 element; that is not done here.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle by the gate + Lean.

`prescribe_haloperidol` is annotated `with Confidence(750)`. Every expression
inside the body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 750/1000.

check can give.

(tacrolimus, Contribution #2). Together they demonstrate that compile-time
epistemic enforcement generalises across drug classes.
